Builds a new CLI verb `viola open`: a new terminal window running a named wrapped session (`viola run` under that name), placed beside its parent's window on Hyprland and left to the window manager elsewhere.
The verb returns only once the session is live, records the window identity and the open's origin in the instance's own state, and takes the calling agent as parent when none is given.
A closed flag allowlist refuses any other flag before anything starts; no shell line is built from the arguments, and the terminal is a direct spawn; logging is codes-only, with no Hyprland reply string in a log line or an error.
Adds to the Hyprland seam a placement dispatch request and a monitors query, recorded and replayed by the fake compositor. It settles the provisional hyprctl read deadline against what the open measures and gives the hyprctl reply bounded-reader row a witness that drives the read past its cap.
Re-verifies at P3, read-only, that the compositor runs dispatch as Lua hl.dsp.*, checking it against the recorded fixtures and the compositor's own help.

body: A new served verb `viola open` added to the CLI surface. It joins viola --help, with its usage line, group label and the served-verbs-only listing.

A refusal of `viola open`: a flag outside the closed allowlist, a missing session name, or a session that never comes live. Each takes the CLI refusal form: an unable line with a kebab-case code word beside a plain word, a hint line and an exit code; faults carry no hint.
Usage errors from clap for `viola open` (an unknown flag, a missing argument) keep CLI exit code 2.
`viola open --json`: one clean document on success, with no hint on failure, under the CLI --json failure-document and fault-body rules.

The human success output of `viola open`: linear and static with no spinner. It carries no SGR off a colour-capable terminal and only beside its word on one, and it uses fixed copy pinned by literal tests.
The session name and the parent name that `viola open` prints are the parsed arguments, with C0/C1 control characters escaped.
Waiting until the session is live falls on the driver, not the human. The wait has a bound with a code-word refusal when it expires, no harsh unwarned timeout, and no time limit on the user.

The hyprctl read deadline is settled against what the open measures. It is a time bound on the driver only, and when it expires the outcome is a code-word refusal or fault, never a bare status or stack trace.

Peer and compositor replies are screened to code words. No window title, class or other Hyprland reply string reaches a log line, a refusal, a fault body or a --json document. thiserror messages for the new errors interpolate nothing.
Every new error body (allowlist refusal, spawn failure, liveness failure, seam failure) has a writer and a test witness in the error-writer census.
Log lines the open emits carry the log identity tags (process, service_name) and codes only.

Socket-directory and home strict-modes failures that the open meets when starting or verifying the session are refused before any frame or write, in the same form as the viola run and revive start refusals.
Opening a terminal for a wrapped session leaves that terminal to the child. The open sends no key and no viola bytes into the session's terminal, and human keystrokes there are never blocked.

The new seam requests (placement dispatch, monitors query) are proved through recorded fixtures replayed by the fake compositor. Live readings never gate a test, and tests sequence on records, not on screen content.
The hyprctl reply bounded-reader row gets a witness that drives the read's stdout drain past its frame cap, replacing the parse-only witness.
If a new event kind or refusal word for the open is added, it gets one hint per code, and the hint names no release.

each new test is deterministic, with zero flakiness, no retries and no skips, and a breach fails the build
each new CLI output-discipline invariant is checked by a literal test in CI, never by a human-only review or a vendor-locked a11y tool

body: The new cli verb's process log: the process-start and process-exit lines of viola open in the cli process-log file, written only under a parsed instance name, with a manual dispatch span for the verb.

Exit codes and process-exit detail codes for open's outcomes (a refused flag, a session that never goes live, a failed spawn, a hyprctl fault): each cause gets its own closed detail code, with no path or pid in it.
The flag-allowlist refusal happens before anything starts. It is a fixed, pathless stderr unable/hint pair, or a --json refusal document, that echoes none of the given argument characters.
The direct terminal spawn is a child spawn log event with its subject. Only environment names are logged, never values, and no argv or shell line is logged.

Codes-only Hyprland logging: no window title, class, address string or other hyprctl reply text reaches a process log line, the detail file, a stderr line or an error Display. Errors from the seam become fixed messages and are logged once, at the boundary.
The hyprctl-probe diag-line subject and the parse-rejected line with parser hyprctl-json (detail words oversize, malformed, unknown-value) as the new dispatch and monitors replies reach them.
The bounded hyprctl reply read: its MAX_FRAME cap on the stdout drain, and the bounded-readers contract witness that drives a read past the cap and sees it refused as oversize.
The hyprctl read deadline (HYPRCTL_DEADLINE, provisional at 5 s) is settled against what open measures. A deadline hit ends in a closed code, never a retry.

The live return: open waits for the session to be live by reading the instance's liveness (its heartbeat and the start events in the events log). The wait is bounded, has no retry-once policy and logs no line per tick.

The new state record of the window identity and the open's origin: persisted by the state crate, carried in the instance's snapshot or events log, and read back through replay, never by a raw snapshot read.
A new events-log event kind for the open, if the chunk adds one. It follows the event line shape and the deterministic-emission rule, and its payload is never copied into a process log.
The parent and the origin names (the calling agent's inherited session name): confined to product surfaces (state, events, list output), never written into a process log line.
Instance resolution for open and its parent: from the given name or the inherited session name, never from the working directory, and never from the window title.
list and list --json, if they show the window identity and origin: the controls in what they render are escaped, and the record's fields are added without renaming the existing ones.

Builds a new CLI verb viola open: a new terminal window, spawned directly with no shell, running a named wrapped session (viola run under that name), placed beside its parent's window on Hyprland and left to the window manager elsewhere.
The verb returns only once the session is live, records the window's identity and the open's origin in the instance's own state, and takes the calling agent's inherited session name as the parent when none is given.

body: The CLI input trust boundary for the new verb: its arguments (session name, parent, flags) are untrusted CLI input checked before anything starts, every name passing the validated viola name type and the shared validators in the core crate.

The closed flag allowlist: a flag outside it is refused before any spawn, read or write, with a fixed refusal word and an exit code from the CLI exit-code table; no shell line is ever built from the given arguments whatever characters they hold, the terminal and the wrapped viola run being direct spawns with each argument one argv element.

The terminal child spawn: the program resolved absolutely rather than through a shell, the child's environment handled as viola run's children are (inherited credentials and parent identity variables stripped where they already are, PATH trust as the plan rules), nothing launched as root, no channel handle inherited by the terminal.

The Hyprland seam's closed request set gains a placement dispatch and a monitors query: each a fixed argv held to a closed shape, no caller-supplied string reaching hyprctl as a command, upstream compositor text treated as content and never as a command.

The hyprctl reply for the new requests: read bounded by the hyprctl deadline and capped at MAX_FRAME, parsed tolerantly with reply text (window title, class, other strings) dropped at the parse, an unknown or unparsable reply failing closed to a code.
The PROVISIONAL hyprctl read deadline is settled against what the open measures: the decision's value and its revisit grounds are re-stated from the measurement, the bound staying a bound.
The bounded-readers census row for the hyprctl reply gets a witness that drives the read's own stdout drain past MAX_FRAME and sees it refused, not a parse-only test.

Codes-only logging under the never-log floor: no window title, class or other Hyprland reply string, no path, pid or id reaches a log line, an error message, stderr or a --json document; error messages interpolate nothing and the full detail goes only to diagnostics.

The new state record of the window identity and the open's origin: written into the instance's own state under the home's owner-only modes and the strict-modes check before use, by the one shared replace helper, read back only after strict modes; the window identity is a closed value, never a reply string, and the self-reported parent and origin authenticate nothing.

The parent default: when no parent is given the calling agent's inherited session name is taken as viola run already reads it, through the name check, an unwrapped session name never becoming a target.

The live return: the verb waits for the session to be live through the existing client seam checks (home strict modes, socket directory, server verification before any frame), bounded in time, and refuses with the existing instance-unreachable causes rather than new free-text ones.

The verb's refusals and errors: fixed code words in human and --json form, no paths, pids, ids or upstream text, the error writer named in the error-writer census, any new refusal word or event kind added in the core crate's closed sets.

Off Hyprland the open still starts the terminal and leaves placement to the window manager; no compositor present is no refusal of the start, and the seam is queried read-only, never to focus, move or close another window.
The security decision entry for v2-08: a new decision naming the argument surface, the closed allowlist and the agent path; a new seam or environment read added by the verb needs its log entry.

Fixtures for the new requests are recorded by the test-only tap with its closed string allowlist, scrubbed or refused whole, reviewed before commit, kept under the fixture hygiene walk, and replayed by the fake compositor; no live window opened or moved and no key sent in the phase.
Test seams the verb's tests need stay under the test-only features, compiled out of the release build; tests use their own home and remove only their own directories.

body: The new viola open verb is a CLI process surface. It is tested as a subprocess, with its human output and its --json output (one document per run) pinned by literals, and a new root integration binary is named with its surface prefix.

The closed flag allowlist: an open carrying any flag outside the allowlist is refused before anything starts (no terminal spawned, no session started, no state written). Each control gets its own negative test.

No shell line is built from the given arguments, whatever they hold: the terminal is a direct argv spawn. Arguments holding shell metacharacters, a leading slash or control characters reach the child unchanged, as argv, and are never interpreted.

Live return: the verb returns only once the opened session is live, as the instance liveness classification reads it. Tests wait on logged events or state, never on sleeps or retries, under a bound below the test kill line.

Parent default: when no parent is given, the open names the calling agent as the parent, taken from the inherited session name the same way viola run reads it. A test-started viola still drops the inherited session variables, except where a test sets one on purpose.

The new instance-state record of window identity and open origin is written by its single writer, with private, owner-only, umask-independent modes. It is read through the snapshot read-or-replay path, is never hand-written by a test and is produced by a real run. If list or list --json shows it, those surfaces' columns and items carry it.

Codes-only logging: no window title, window class or other Hyprland reply string reaches a process log line, an event, an error body or a human error line. Error bodies hold no upstream text or path, and thiserror messages interpolate nothing.
Every new product error writer the verb adds is named in the error-writer census, and its error body is covered by a surface witness.

New Hyprland requests (a placement dispatch over exec and a monitors query) join the seam's closed request set. Each has an argv measured live, a recording made by viola-hypr-tap, and a byte-for-byte replay by the fake compositor. Tests reach the compositor only through that fake or a real stub executable, never a live compositor in CI.

The terminal the open spawns is an external process. In tests it is a real stub executable on a test-scoped PATH, never a mock of unowned code and never a real window. The tests open, move, focus and close no window on the host.

The hyprctl reply read is a bounded external reader that keeps its frame cap. Its Boundary row gets a witness that drives the read's own stdout drain past MAX_FRAME and sees it refused, plus a remove-the-guard witness. A parse test of a frame at the cap is not enough.
The HYPRCTL_DEADLINE read deadline is settled against what viola open measures. Tests drive the deadline through an injected clock or the product constant, and never through test-owned real time.

The parse of a new monitors reply, and any new parser the open adds, is a parser surface: it gets property tests with committed seeds, a fuzz corpus with replay, and is held to the tolerant, forward-compatible reading of unknown fields.
Recorded Hyprland fixtures are scrubbed of real data (home paths, usernames, real window titles), use synthetic text, are checked against their schema, and are kept per compositor version.
Off Hyprland, the open still starts the terminal and leaves placement to the window manager. That case is reached through the absent or failed compositor seam.

Any new event kind or refusal word added to the closed core enums changes only by decision. It keeps the event line's format and keys, the code-word format, the log event corr field, and the tolerant reader's handling of an unknown word.

Opening runs viola run under the name. That start's own checks (strict modes, the socket directory, already-live and stale-heartbeat start refusals) keep their order, and the open's exit and refusal surface reports them by their existing causes and exit codes.
The Hyprland seam crate stays a sync crate: no tokio in its normal graph, and it compiles alone without features. It is the seam's first product caller, linked from the root bin.

Re-verification, read-only: the claim that the compositor version 0.56.2 runs dispatch as Lua is read back against the recorded fixtures and the compositor's help. It is recorded as a reading, never as verification.
Human-mode output of viola open escapes control characters, carries no SGR without a terminal and shows names as list rows do. The new verb joins the grouped verb table of viola --help.

each new test helper exists once and is shared, never copied between test binaries
